title: The paratransit invoice SFMTA’s review missed

beats.text: A San Francisco audit found 16 hours that a paratransit broker should never have billed.

visual.sub: A payroll check found 16 hours the broker should not have billed

beats.text: The overcharge was $644.94. The broker said it would credit the next bill.
A shopping cart printout was offered as proof for office supplies.

visual.kicker: A payroll check found 16 hours the broker should not have billed

beats.text: The agency also paid $12,000 in incentives without checking the underlying data.

visual.kicker: Timing bonuses and trip counts used different records

beats.text: Two timing calculations were wrong. They did not change what the broker earned.

visual.kicker: Timing bonuses and trip counts used different records

beats.text: The scheduling system counted more trips than the invoices. Only validated rides were billed.

visual.kicker: Timing bonuses and trip counts used different records

beats.text: In January 2014, two accounts were still open, eight months after closure requests.

visual.kicker: Two requests to close accounts remained outstanding

beats.text: Auditors linked neither account to improper payments.

visual.kicker: Two requests to close accounts remained outstanding

beats.text: The original fee printed in the agreement was $674,277.
The appendix showed a higher fee. The signed amendment corrected the clause and added transport duties.

visual.kicker: The signed amendment resolves a historical contract mismatch

beats.text: By April 2015, the Controller said 36 of 42 recommendations were implemented.
The specific invoice credit remains unverified.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
